title: Deal heuristics handoff notes (draft)
summary: Working notes for an ultra-compact handoff playbook for sellers and SEs running pilots. Focus: quick heuristics to choose deployment option, fallback scripts, immediate canary checks, and short slide set for a 5-minute technical sync. Draft contains rough scripts, slide outline, open questions and next steps.
audience: Field sales, Sales Engineering, Solutions Architects, GTM ops
purpose: Create a 1-page mental model sellers can use during discovery + a 5-slide technical handoff for pilots. Minimize back-and-forth with infra teams by giving clear thresholds and quick remediation steps.
slide_outline: Slide 1 — 60s: Value hook + recommended deployment (hosted vs dedicated vs private)
Slide 2 — Risk map: latency, cost, data sensitivity (3x3 quick scoring)
Slide 3 — Canary plan: traffic slices, test prompts, success gates (latency+quality)
Slide 4 — Fallback ladder: compatible models + routing policy examples
Slide 5 — Next steps: POC checklist, required stakeholder signoffs, timeline
quick_scripts: Discovery opener: 'Quick question — do you need consistent p50 latency under 150ms for customer experiences, or is p99 predictability more important? That helps me pick hosted vs dedicated.'

Objection: 'We’re worried about cost' -> Response: 'We can start on hosted API with token caps and auto-scaling; if traffic regularizes we’ll recommend a Dedicated commitment after 30 days. I’ll share an estimated cross-over model for your query distribution.'

Security objection: 'Can you do VPC/on‑prem?' -> Response: 'Yes — we’ll scope Private deployment. For pilots, we usually prototype on a VPC with sanitized data and run an eval on your prompts to validate before an on‑prem effort.'

Canary script prompt sanity check: 'Run 5 representative production prompts at X tokens, measure end‑to‑end latency and token cost; verify no hallucination regressions using the subset of golden responses.'
fallback_matrix: Primary: rwd-compat-v2 (best latency/cost for short-context chat)
Fallback 1: rwd-quant-micro (slightly lower quality, 2x throughput per GPU)
Fallback 2: open-compat-lite (public open model, lower cost but higher latency variability)
Routing rule example: prefer Primary in region A, and if p95 > SLO for 2 consecutive minutes, route 20% traffic to Fallback 1 and notify SE
pilot-checklist: Define 3 'must-pass' prompts (one short, one long, one edge case)
Agree SLOs: p50 latency / p95 latency / token cost target
Decide deployment mode: HOSTED/Dedicated/Private (include cost sensitivity)
Assign owners: SE (canary runs), Infra (routing), Customer (test data access)
Run baseline eval and attach results to Confluence page
handoff_talking_points: Keep the first technical sync to 15 minutes: 5min seller context, 5min SE run-through, 5min actions
When handing to Platform, include expected QPS, median tokens per request, and golden prompts
Call out any regulatory constraints up front (PII, retention, region restriction) — these change the deployment decision immediately
If customer asks for SLA now, explain reserved capacity path (Dedicated) and quick estimate for capacity commit
open_questions: What exact token threshold should trigger recommending Dedicated vs staying Hosted for midmarket (need metric from finance) — ACTION: Marco to ask pricing ops
Do we have a canned way to simulate prefix caching benefits for a pilot? If not, note in handoff that initial numbers will understate steady-state cost savings
Agree on notification cadence when fallbacks kick in (Slack vs email vs PagerDuty)
notes_to_self: Keep language compact for slides; remove any heavy infra jargon. Add an appendix with example request/response traces if this doc survives draft. Validate fallback model names with runtime team (Benji).
